newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein steady, demand up.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein steady, demand up.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were steady in late trading on Monday, with buying interest improving after the May 29 general election, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,415 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, compared with 1,410-15 rupiah at the opening. Crude palm oil was last done at 1,240 rupiah and 1,243 rupiah at tenders in the North Sumatran capital of Medan last Wednesday.
"The market was certainly more active than it was last week," one trader said. "Trading would have been more active had it not been for falls in Malaysia."
"I think prices will continue to be steady tomorrow on expectations of better demand," the trader said.
Traders said market activity was generally expected to pick up after last Thursday's elections, which saw President Suharto's ruling Golkar party romping home to a landslide win.
Trading had been subdued during the 27-day campaign which was marred by the worst political violence in three decades.
"Now that the elections are over, the market should be returning to normal," another trader said. "But I think it will take at least two weeks for the market to find its feet."
